adds a third extended term of five years to the lease

conditions.source:
The council convened to finalize pending appointments and review reports from the Civic Development, Public Assets, and Native Communities Committee. The assembly first addressed a series of appointments, with members voting to confirm them. The motion to confirm the appointments carried, and the appointments were officially ratified.

Following the appointments, the committee presented its report on Agenda Item 17, specifically Bill 119648. This bill relates to Seattle Parks and Recreation and authorizes the superintendent to amend an existing ten-year lease with the Seattle Children’s Play Garden. The proposed amendment adds a third extended term of five years to the lease. The committee recommended that the council pass the ordinance.

Councilmember Suarez spoke in support of the bill, noting that the program expands recreational opportunities for children with physical challenges. She highlighted that the facility is located at Coleman Playfield, which she described as an ideal site for specialized recreational development. She emphasized the value of public assets in the community and reiterated the committee’s recommendation for passage.

After the presentation, the clerk called for questions or comments, but none were recorded. The council then proceeded to a vote on the passage of the bill. The roll call vote resulted in six members voting in favor and no members voting opposed. Consequently, the bill was passed. The session concluded with the confirmation of the appointments and the approval of the lease amendment for the Seattle Children’s Play Garden.
